At $23,950, Would You Become A Cars & Coffee Legend In This 2012 Roush Stage 2 Mustang GT?

CA
By Chloe Adams Car Culture & Restomod Editor • via Jalopnik Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Jalopnik Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • With its Roush Stage Two appearance and handling package, today's Nice Price or No Dice Mustang GT certainly talks the talk.
  • Though it's unmodified from factory specs, the 5.0-liter Coyote V8 under the hood ensures it walks the walk, too.
  • Let's see if its price has you walking away.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • CHLOE ADAMS Car Culture & Restomod Editor

Heritage Preservation vs Modern Performance

Automotive passion is increasingly defined by the synthesis of analog soul and contemporary engineering. This coverage from Jalopnik illustrates how bespoke builders, private collectors, and restomod artists are preserving the golden eras of internal combustion while adopting carbon fiber composites and precision craftsmanship.

Big Picture: Auction hammer prices and enthusiast demand indicate sustained historical appreciation for rare, analog driver's vehicles.

With its Roush Stage Two appearance and handling package, today's Nice Price or No Dice Mustang GT certainly talks the talk. Though it's unmodified from factory specs, the 5.0-liter Coyote V8 under the hood ensures it walks the walk, too. Let's see if its price has you walking away.

📌 The Core Development

According to biblical lore, 666 is said to be "the number of the beast," an identifier of a bad motor scooter whose arrival signals the end of days. Or maybe it's actually 616? That's the number found in the earliest known writings of the biblical Book of Revelation: the Ephraemi Rescriptus and Papyrus 115, also known as the Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus. Given the seriousness implied by this 666 individual's arrival, we might want to clarify that.

While it's just one number off from being half of 666, the 2002 Volkswagen GTI 337 (named for the internal VW code for the original GTI) we looked at on Tuesday didn't come close to being half bad. Unfortunately for its seller, however, few of you found anything good in its $13,337 price tag. When all was said and done, that fell in an 80% 'No Dice' loss

🔍 Background & Sector Context

When the Ford Motor Company introduced the Mustang on April 17 th , 1964, it didn't just create an instant hit that defined a new category and became the marque's brand ambassador for decades to come. With that launch, the company also set the stage for a cottage industry of Mustang modifiers. Obviously, the best-known is Carroll Shelby, whose namesake GT-Number models turned Ford's pony from secretary specials into real race cars. Others, including Steve Saleen, Steeda Autosports, and racing legend Jack Roush, have put their mark on the Mustang over the years.

According to its ad, this 2012 Ford Mustang GT is one of 105 Roush Stage 2 cars built for that model year. The Stage 2 mods include visual changes: rocker stripes, a white-and-gray hood appliqué, louvers over the side lights, front and rear spoilers, and RS2 (Roush Stage 2) badging. The interior features white-faced gauges and Jack Roush signature embroidery on the bucket seat backs.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

The Roush riot doesn't stop at the aesthetics, either. Underneath, the car has been massaged with stiffer springs and revised suspension geometry for tauter handling. Putting the power to the pavement is a set of 20-inch alloys wrapped in low-profile rubber that looks to have plenty of tread left.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

In the RS2, Roush left the drivetrain untouched. That's okay, though, since this model year's GT sported Ford's mad-modular Coyote 5.0 V8, an engine that, despite being naturally aspirated, makes a stout 412 horsepower and 390 pound-feet of torque. That's properly routed through a six-speed manual and, according to the seller, a one-piece driveshaft installed by a previous owner feeding the limited-slip rear end. This was the last Mustang to offer the comforting simplicity of a live rear axle.

The previous owner also installed a short-shift kit and long-tube headers. The seller avers that the car is "very fun to drive" and has been "well cared for." Currently, it has 41,000 miles on the clock and comes with a clean title. It's well known that Mustang GTs enjoy a reputation for car event exit shenanigans that often end with an introduction to a curb, tree, or unsuspecting bystander. It would be a shame to let his car's clean presentation meet that fate.
